assignment:
Your principal is considering changing school policy so that students may not participate in sports or other activities unless they have at least a grade B average. Many students have a grade C average. 
She would like to hear the students' views on this possible policy change. Write a letter to your principal arguing for or against requiring at least a grade B average to participate in sports or other activities. Be sure to support your arguments with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I think you should not make students keep a B average to be in sports and other activities. A grade rule might seem like it helps students study more, but it would mostly hurt the kids who need help the most.

A lot of students with a C average are only struggling in one or two classes. For them, sports, band, or debate is often the reason they come to school. If you take those activities away, you also take away the structure that could help their grades get better.

Activities also teach things that classrooms do not always test, like teamwork and handling pressure. Students who learn these things often go back to homework with more focus. Some kids are very stressed about grades, but a team can help them feel less alone.

Instead of cutting students off, the school could offer tutoring, study halls, or check-ins for anyone whose grades drop. That would help them instead.

Please think about this.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I think we should not require a B average to be in sports and other activities. Some people say it will make students study more, but I think it would hurt the kids who need help the most.

A lot of students with a C average are only struggling in one or two classes. They are not failing everything. For those kids, sports, band, or debate is usually the reason they come to school and keep trying. It is where they make friends with teachers and other students. If you take that away, you also take away the thing that could help their grades get better.

Activities also teach things that tests do not really measure, like working on a team, managing your time, and staying calm when things get stressful. A lot of students come back to their homework with more focus after learning those things.

Instead of kicking students out of activities, the school could offer tutoring, study halls, or check-ins with teachers for anyone whose grades start to drop. That would help the struggling students instead of shutting them out.

Thank you for listening to what students think.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
